\chapter{Not Feeling Well}
\label{ch:ml-not-feeling-well}
\hlchaptermodality{115}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I have a cold, a headache or dizziness, that I am not well, and that I need rest.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 115: i can say I have a cold, a headache or dizziness, that I am not well, and that I need rest.

\section[jaladōṣaṁ]{\ml{ജലദോഷം} (jaladōṣaṁ) — a cold}

\label{lesson:ML-C115-cold}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a cough, then the Malayalam for a fever.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ജലദോഷം}}
\textbf{\ml{ജലദോഷം}} (\emph{jaladōṣaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cold\textquotedblright{}, the kind with a runny nose.

\textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ജലദോഷമുണ്ട്}} (\emph{enikkŭ jaladōṣamuṇṭŭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}I have a cold\textquotedblright{}. The person sits in \textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്}}, \textquotedblleft{}to me\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ട്}} says \textquotedblleft{}there is\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An illness, said with to-me and there-is.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jaladōṣaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jaladōṣaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{enikkŭ jaladōṣamuṇṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a cough, then the Malayalam for a fever, then say \emph{jaladōṣaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ജലദോഷം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cold\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[talavēdana]{\ml{തലവേദന} (talavēdana) — a headache}

\label{lesson:ML-C115-headache}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a fever, then the Malayalam for a cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തലവേദന}}
\textbf{\ml{തലവേദന}} (\emph{talavēdana}) — \textquotedblleft{}a headache\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ml{തല}} (\emph{tala}), \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\ml{വേദന}} (\emph{vēdana}), \textquotedblleft{}pain\textquotedblright{}, which you already know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two known words make a new one.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talavēdana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talavēdana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{enikkŭ talavēdanayuṇṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a fever, then the Malayalam for a cold, then say \emph{talavēdana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തലവേദന} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A headache\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[viśramaṁ]{\ml{വിശ്രമം} (viśramaṁ) — rest}

\label{lesson:ML-C115-rest}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a cold, then the Malayalam for a headache.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വിശ്രമം}}
\textbf{\ml{വിശ്രമം}} (\emph{viśramaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}rest\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ml{വിശ്രമിക്കൂ}} (\emph{viśramikkū}) — \textquotedblleft{}please rest\textquotedblright{}, what you tell a friend who is unwell.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The answer to a cold and a headache.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśramaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśramaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} tell a friend \emph{viśramikkū}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a cold, then the Malayalam for a headache, then say \emph{viśramaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വിശ്രമം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Rest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[sukhamilla]{\ml{സുഖമില്ല} (sukhamilla) — not well}

\label{lesson:ML-C115-notwell}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for rest, then the Malayalam for dizziness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സുഖമില്ല}}
\textbf{\ml{സുഖമില്ല}} (\emph{sukhamilla}) — \textquotedblleft{}(I'm) not well\textquotedblright{}, \textbf{\ml{സുഖം}} (\emph{sukhaṁ}), \textquotedblleft{}well-being\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\ml{ഇല്ല}} (\emph{illa}), \textquotedblleft{}there isn't\textquotedblright{}. It answers \textbf{\ml{സുഖമാണോ}?}, \textquotedblleft{}are you well?\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The honest answer to sukhamāṇō.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sukhamilla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sukhamilla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sukhamilla}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for rest, then the Malayalam for dizziness, then say \emph{sukhamilla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സുഖമില്ല} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Not well\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
